The test image shows a mango leaf that is dried, brown, and appears to be rolled or curled. This indicates a "leaf" plant part is affected.

Now I will read the `part_index.md` file to see which diseases affect the "leaf" part.

thought
The reference image for Die_Back (Mango_Leaf_166.jpg) shows a completely dried, brown, and rolled leaf, which is highly consistent with the test image. This strongly suggests Die_Back.

Next, I will view a reference image for Anthracnose to compare.

thought
The reference image for Anthracnose (Mango_Leaf_14.jpg) shows a leaf with irregular holes and damage, but it's not uniformly dried, brown, or rolled like the test image. This makes Anthracnose less likely than Die_Back.

Next, I will view a reference image for Powdery_Mildew. Since no symptom description was provided for it, I'll rely purely on the visual.

thought
The reference image for Powdery_Mildew (Mango_Leaf_14.jpg) clearly shows white, powdery patches on a green leaf. This is distinctly different from the dried, brown, and rolled leaf in the test image. Therefore, Powdery_Mildew is not a match.

Finally, I will view a reference image for Sooty_Mould.

The reference image for Sooty_Mould (Mango_Leaf_147.jpg) shows dark, sooty, superficial deposits on a leaf, consistent with the symptom description. This is clearly different from the dried, brown, and rolled leaf in the test image. Therefore, Sooty_Mould is not a match.

Based on the symptom descriptions and the comparison with the four reference images, the test image most closely matches the characteristics of Die_Back. The rolled, brown, and dried appearance of the test image is highly consistent with the Die_Back symptom "Leaves roll upward and turn brown with a scorch-like appearance, then drop". The Die_Back reference image also showed a very similar dried, brown, and rolled leaf. The other classes (Anthracnose, Powdery_Mildew, Sooty_Mould) show distinct visual symptoms (irregular holes, white powdery growth, dark sooty deposits, respectively) that are not present in the test image.
